title: CRA-SME Toolkit: a risk-driven, evidence-based research toolkit for EU Cyber Resilience Act implementation in SMEs
description:
Research toolkit for implementing and evaluating the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) in small and medium-sized enterprises.

Contents: a 46-obligation CRA requirements catalogue (CSV) with references, application dates and evidence types; a risk and evidence workbook (xlsx, v1.0 for comparison and corrected v1.2); the crasme Python package (ordinal and Monte Carlo risk models, inter-rater agreement statistics, SBOM and vulnerability-scanner accuracy metrics, Article 14 reporting clocks and tabletop scoring, traceability, product and release-decision JSON Schemas, an evidence provenance manifest); a SHA-pinned GitHub Actions evidence workflow; protocols, pre-registration template and data-collection templates for eight experiments (E1-E8); seven executed Jupyter notebooks; a pilot SBOM generator benchmark (real tool output, 3 fixtures); a review of toolkit v1.0; and a comparison with existing solutions and related work.

New in 1.2.0: fail-safe scanner execution-status records; a single release-decision engine (PASS / FAIL / REVIEW_REQUIRED with reason codes) bound to product, version, build SHA and artifact digest; legal-review metadata on every catalogue row (all unverified pending legal review); lifecycle and Article 14 templates; anchored risk scoring; evidence-data governance and redaction; E3 allocation and analysis scripts; and a 69-fault seeded evaluation including faults from an independent adversarial review (false-green rate 0/69 vs 63/69 for v1.1).

Data status: only experiments/e1_sbom_benchmark/pilot-results/ contains real tool output. All other example and notebook data are synthetic and labelled as such.

Limits: research instruments only; not legal advice, not an official CRA assessment and not a conformity assessment. Risk scores are not CRA criteria.

Licensing: code under Apache-2.0; documentation, templates, catalogue, workbooks and notebook text under CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSES/ and README).
notes: Version 1.2.0 (research edition). Synthetic data is labelled. The obligation catalogue is legally unverified; see docs/v1.2-implementation-status.md.
